hypothesis: If oceanic islands hold fewer species than equal-area continental regions, species richness is lower on oceanic islands than on continental regions of the same area.
pass_criterion: Across area-matched bins, median native plant species richness on oceanic islands is at least 30% lower than on continental regions, with a one-sided Mann–Whitney p < 0.01.
fail_criterion: Median richness on oceanic islands is not lower by at least 30% in area-matched bins, or the difference has p ≥ 0.05.
interpretation: 'Species of all kinds' cannot be tested across all taxa in one dataset. This plan uses native vascular plant richness from regional checklists as a proxy. 'Equal continental areas' becomes area-matched bins. Oceanic islands are those flagged as never connected to a continent. Any residual dependence on physical conditions is not tested.

dataset.name: GIFT – Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.publisher: University of Göttingen, Biodiversity, Macroecology and Biogeography
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT has regional plant checklists with area, geology/island type and native species counts, accessible through an R package. Richness is compared between oceanic island and mainland units in area bins.
